name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+22 district lean in heavily Republican southwest Virginia
Griffith's large financial advantage ($1.1M cash vs $89K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~2%
Incumbent running with no polling or expert attention suggesting vulnerability
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively to Griffith: a deep R+22 district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge, with markets pricing a Democratic win at just 2%. No polls or ratings indicate any competitive threat, so the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Griffith or an unexpectedly strong Democratic environment in Virginia could narrow the margin, though a flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan Griffith is seeking another term in a southwest Virginia district that leans Republican by more than twenty points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, holding over $1 million in cash after raising more than $2 million, while Democrat Joy Powers has raised under $250,000. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged in the race.

Prediction markets give Griffith roughly a 97% chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings suggest the seat is in play. The district's strong partisan lean and incumbency advantages make this a Safe Republican race, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
